description: Team building "The Earth Information Jukebox": NASA Earth data you can HEAR, not just see, made for blind and low-vision users and curious people worldwide. Our sound reflects real scientific values, and we'll demo it with eyes closed. We build with AI tools, with curiosity and a sense of humor. Looking for audio/sound design or accessibility/UX skills. Beginners welcome!
summary: Earth Is Speaking turns NASA Earth visualizations into sound so anyone, including blind and low-vision people, can explore our planet by ear. Touch the map, use the keyboard or say a place: low notes mean cold air, high notes hot air, rising tones more night lights, drum rhythms lightning. Six NASA SVS products (GEOS-FP temperature, Black Marble night lights, ECCO-2 ocean currents, GEOS aerosols, GEDI forest height, ISS LIS lightning) are decoded against NASA's official color bars and played in real time with fixed, honest rules. It includes a narrated journey from Antarctica to Lima, voice commands, an audio-only mode, English and Spanish, playlists and sound postcards. Built in Lima, Peru.
details: Accessible web app that sonifies 6 NASA SVS visualizations. Python scripts match every pixel to NASA's official color bar (99.1% match) and the browser plays each value as a pentatonic note with the Web Audio API (no AI in the sound). Features: search 242 countries with area-weighted summaries and compare, guided narrated journey, voice search and commands, audio-only mode, keyboard and screen reader support, visual pulse for deaf users, EN/ES, My Earth Song playlists, WAV download, shareable sound postcards. Honest labels (approx., trend, category, ~20 km per pixel). Tools: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Web Audio API, Web Speech API, Python, NumPy, Pillow, FFmpeg, Natural Earth, GitHub Pages, axe-core. Code and texts written with AI assistance (Claude), reviewed by the team.
